reason: User-supplied parameter flows directly to bar via doSomething unless length > 1. The replacement logic replaces characters starting at index (len - "Z".length()). Since "Z" has length 1, the start index becomes len-1, replacing only the last character with Z. If the input contains XSS payloads longer than 1 char (e.g., "><script>alert(1)</script>) they remain intact except possibly the very last byte, allowing script execution.

evidence.note: Input param flows to bar; replace call uses param.length()-1 as start index, leaving most of payload unchanged
